questions.q: The components of the spine are:
opts: Musculoskeletal: vertebral column; Neurological: spinal cord + spinal nerves
questions.exp: Spine components: musculoskeletal: vertebral column; neurological: spinal cord + spinal nerves. (Book p173)

questions.q: The vertebrae are classified as:
questions.exp: Vertebrae: cervical (C), thoracic (T)/dorsal (D), lumbar (L), sacral (S). (Book p173)

questions.q: The intervertebral disc is made of:
questions.exp: Intervertebral disc: annulus fibrosus and nucleus pulposus. (Book p173)

questions.q: The functions of the intervertebral disc include:
opts: Segments the spine (increased mobility) and acts as a shock absorber
questions.exp: Functions: segments the spine (increased mobility); shock absorber. (Book p173)

questions.q: A fracture of the pars inter-articularis is called:
questions.exp: Pars inter-articularis: fracture (spondylolysis) -> spondylolisthesis (slipping of one vertebra over another). (Book p173)

questions.q: Spondylolisthesis means:
opts: Slipping of one vertebra over another
questions.exp: Spondylolisthesis: slipping of one vertebra over another. (Book p173)

questions.q: The articular facets articulate to:
questions.exp: Articular facets: articulates to keep the spine aligned. (Book p173)

questions.q: Denis' concept of spine stability is based on:
questions.exp: Denis' concept of spine stability: based on 3 columns of vertebra. (Book p173)

questions.q: The anterior column of the spine includes:
opts: Anterior longitudinal ligament, anterior annulus, anterior 2/3rd of vertebral body
questions.exp: Anterior column: anterior longitudinal ligament, anterior annulus, anterior 2/3rd of vertebral body. (Book p173)

questions.q: The middle column of the spine includes:
opts: Posterior 1/3rd of vertebral body, posterior annulus, posterior longitudinal ligament
questions.exp: Middle column: posterior 1/3rd of vertebral body, posterior annulus, posterior longitudinal ligament. (Book p173)

questions.q: The posterior column of the spine includes:
opts: Posterior elements (pedicles, facets, lamina, spinous process) and posterior ligaments
questions.exp: Posterior column: posterior elements (pedicles, facets, lamina, spinous process); posterior ligaments. (Book p173)

questions.q: An injury involving only 1 column of the spine is:
questions.exp: Clinical aspect: injury involving 1 column -> stable injury; Rx: conservative. (Book p174)

questions.q: An injury involving 2 or more columns of the spine is:
questions.exp: Injury involving 2 or more columns -> unstable injury; Rx: stabilization / fixation (surgery). (Book p174)

questions.q: The m/c site of vertebral fracture is:
questions.exp: M/c site: vertebral fracture: lower thoracic (T12). (Book p174)

questions.q: The m/c site of vertebral dislocation is the:
questions.exp: M/c site: vertebral dislocation: cervical spine. (Book p174)

questions.q: The cervical spine is prone to dislocation d/t:
opts: Ligamentous stabilizers > bony, and horizontal arrangement of articular facets
questions.exp: Cervical spine d/t: stabilizers: ligamentous > bony; horizontal arrangement of articular facets. (Book p174)

questions.q: The lumbar spine has a vertical arrangement of articular facets, which gives:
questions.exp: Lumbar spine: vertical arrangement of articular facets -> increased risk of fracture > dislocation. (Book p174)

questions.q: The highest risk of spinal cord injury is with:
questions.exp: Highest risk of spinal cord injury: cervical spine fracture. (Book p174)

questions.q: Immediate management in cervical spine injury is:
opts: Turn patient onto their back, support placed behind neck, transported to nearest hospital
questions.exp: Note: 1. turn patient onto their back; 2. support placed behind neck; 3. transported to nearest hospital. (Book p174)

questions.q: Jefferson's fracture is the m/c fracture of the:
questions.exp: Jefferson's / C1 vertebral (atlas) fracture: m/c fracture on C1 vertebra. (Book p175)

questions.q: The mechanism of injury in Jefferson's fracture is:
opts: Axial loading / compression - fragments burst out away from spinal canal
questions.exp: Mechanism of injury: axial loading / compression; fragments burst out away from spinal canal. (Book p175)

questions.q: A characteristic feature of Jefferson's fracture is:
questions.exp: Jefferson's fracture: no neurological deficits. (Book p175)

questions.q: Investigations in Jefferson's fracture include:
opts: X-ray (open mouth view) and CT scan (best)
questions.exp: Investigations: X-ray (open mouth view); CT scan (best). (Book p175)

questions.q: A stable Jefferson's fracture is treated:
questions.exp: Treatment: stable fracture: conservative. (Book p175)

questions.q: An unstable Jefferson's fracture (torn transverse ligament) is treated with:
questions.exp: Unstable: surgery (atlanto-occipital fusion). (Book p175)

questions.q: The types of C2 vertebral (axis) fracture are:
opts: Odontoid fracture (m/c fracture of C2) and Hangman's fracture
questions.exp: Types: odontoid fracture: m/c fracture of C2; Hangman's fracture. (Book p175)

questions.q: Hangman's fracture is a fracture of the:
opts: Pars inter-articularis of C2 vertebra (spondylolysis of C2)
questions.exp: Hangman's fracture: fracture of pars inter-articularis of C2 vertebra (spondylolysis of C2). (Book p175)

questions.q: Hangman's fracture causes:
questions.exp: Hangman's fracture causes dislocation of C2 over C3 (spondylolisthesis). (Book p175)

questions.q: In Hangman's fracture, the neurological status is typically:
questions.exp: Hangman's fracture: no neurological deficit. (Book p175)

questions.q: The m/c cause of Hangman's fracture is:
questions.exp: M/c cause: RTA > hanging. (Book p175)

questions.q: Whiplash injury is a:
questions.exp: Whiplash injury: soft tissue injury. (Book p175)

questions.q: The mechanism of whiplash injury is:
questions.exp: Mechanism: hyperextension -> flexion. (Book p175)

questions.q: Features of whiplash injury include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Features: chronic neck pain; no neurological deficits; normal X-ray / CT scan. (Book p175)

questions.q: Treatment of whiplash injury is:
questions.exp: Rx: cervical collar. (Book p175)

questions.q: Clay Shoveler's fracture results from shoveling with strong contraction of paraspinal and upper limb muscles, causing:
questions.exp: Clay Shoveler's fracture: shoveling -> strong contraction of paraspinal and upper limb muscles -> avulsion of C7 spinous process. (Book p176)

questions.q: The Chance (jack-knife / seat-belt) fracture was described by:
questions.exp: Chance / jack-knife / seat-belt fracture: described by Dr. G.G. Chance. (Book p176)

questions.q: In Chance fracture, a complete transverse splitting of the vertebra is called:
questions.exp: Complete transverse splitting of: vertebra: bony Chance; ligament and disc: soft tissue Chance. (Book p176)

questions.q: The mechanism of injury in Chance fracture is:
opts: Seatbelts without shoulder harnesses -> flexion of spine at lumbar vertebra -> complete transection of spinal cord (involves all 3 columns: unstable fracture) -> paraplegia
questions.exp: Mechanism: seatbelts without shoulder harnesses; flexion of spine at lumbar vertebra; complete transection of spinal cord (involves all 3 columns: unstable fracture); paraplegia. (Book p176)

questions.q: Treatment of Chance fracture is:
questions.exp: Rx: stabilization and surgery. (Book p176)

questions.q: The causative factor of a compression fracture is:
questions.exp: Causative factor: compression fracture: osteoporosis. (Book p176)

questions.q: The causative factor of a burst fracture is:
questions.exp: Causative factor: burst fracture: significant trauma. (Book p176)

questions.q: The mechanism of a compression fracture is:
questions.exp: Mechanism: compression fracture: flexion -> compression. (Book p176)

questions.q: The mechanism of a burst fracture is:
questions.exp: Mechanism: burst fracture: axial loading. (Book p176)

questions.q: The characteristic feature of a compression fracture is:
opts: Wedgeing of vertebra (anterior column shortened, posterior column maintained)
Bursting of posterior wall into canal
questions.exp: Compression fracture: wedgeing of vertebra (anterior column shortened, posterior column maintained). (Book p176)

questions.q: The characteristic feature of a burst fracture is:
questions.exp: Burst fracture: convex anterior and posterior walls. (Book p176)

questions.q: SCIWORA stands for:
opts: Spinal cord injury without radiographic abnormality
Spinal column injury with radiographic abnormality
questions.exp: SCIWORA: spinal cord injury without radiographic abnormality. (Book p177)
